newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Golf-Westwood recovers from shaky start to retain lead.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Westwood recovers from shaky start to retain lead.

text.p: Young Englishman Lee Westwood produced another battling display after losing his Irish Open lead briefly on Saturday, to lead the event at Druid's Glen for a third day.
Westwood takes a three-stroke lead into Sunday's final round but had to fightback for the second straight day after falling behind early when he dropped three shots over his first seven holes.

Five birdies in seven holes from the eighth, however, took him to a round of one-under-par 70 and a total of nine-under-par 204, three strokes ahead of the defending champion Colin Montgomerie of Scotland who hit a 69.
Two late dropped shots, though, reduced Westwood's lead and kept Montgomerie within striking distance of a possible second Irish title in a row.

"I got off to a bad start again and I won't want to be doing that for a third day because Monty will be a danger," said Westwood, who will seal a place in the European Ryder Cup team with a victory here.
"He's the best player in Europe, nearly in the world, so he is bound to be a great threat. But he's starting three behind and it's nice to know that such a good field here is even further behind."
It proved a disappointing day for the two Scandinavians who began the third round only two shots behind Westwood.
Denmark's Thomas Bjorn dropped back to joint fourth place on 210 after running up a quadruple-bogey eight on the toughest hole on the Druid's Glen course, the 13th.
Swede Michael Jonzon dropped to 211 after hitting two double-bogeys, including one at the unlucky 13th.
England's David Tapping, who landed a hole-in-one on Friday, moved up to third on 209.
Spain's Jose Maria Olazabal fired the best round of the day, holing six birdies in a round of 65 to move to three-under-par 210.
